item.title: Cambridge Gardens, 5th September
item.description:
Every Saturday, unlicensed street vendors set up around the St Augustine’s School car boot sale, selling unwanted goods on the surrounding streets. There are also concerns that some goods may be stolen. At the end of the day, large quantities of unwanted clothing, rubbish and unsold items are simply abandoned, leaving the surrounding streets in a considerable mess. This is not an isolated incident - it happens repeatedly every Saturday and has become a predictable consequence of the car boot sale. “Illegal Street Trading” signs have been installed in the area, but they appear to have had virtually no deterrent effect. Traders continue to return week after week. The issue now requires active enforcement rather than signage alone. The organisers of the car boot sale and the council should also consider how the event is contributing to activity outside the official site and the resulting impact on local residents and the surrounding streets. Residents should not be left dealing with the rubbish and deterioration of the local environment every weekend as an external cost of a commercially operated event.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Cambridge Gardens, London
Report on FixMyStreet
